subject: SLA amendment: batched inference uptime floor and monthly credit cap
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@brightline.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: 2028-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SLA floor adjustment for batched inference pilot

Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the engine handled our batched traffic really well. Before we spin up the pilot in prod, procurement raised a question on the SLA wording. Our workload is heavily batched and occasional cold-start KV-cache spikes are expected. We can't commit to a 99.9% uptime floor for the pilot; our internal risk team needs a lower floor (99.5%) for the first three months.

Specific ask:
- Temporary uptime floor of 99.5% (pilot period: 90 days)
- Monthly service credit that scales if we fall below that floor; cap at 20% of monthly invoice for pilot months
- Explicit maintenance carveouts for rolling infra updates (we can accept up to 8 hours/month regionally)

I've attached a simple worksheet that shows our expected request and an initial credit cap we modeled. Can Redwood sign off on a provisional amendment to the standard SLA for the pilot window? If needed, we can loop in legal.

Jordan
Jordan Ellis | Head of Platform Engineering
Brightline Systems
Attachment: Brightline_SLA_Request.xlsx (worksheet: requested floors + invoice model)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@brightline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA floor adjustment for batched inference pilot

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear ask and the worksheet. Short answer: we can support a provisional SLA amendment for a time-boxed pilot, but we want to balance availability guarantees with predictable economic exposure. High level proposal from our side:

- Pilot uptime floor: 99.5% for the 90-day pilot window (matches your request).
- Remedy (monthly service credit): tiered scaling starting at 5% credit for availability 99.0–99.49%, 12% for 98.0–98.99%, and 20% for <98.0%. Cap at 20% of the monthly invoice for pilot months.
- Maintenance carveouts: we will exclude scheduled rolling maintenance if notified 48 hours in advance; incidental emergency maintenance will be exempt if we provide post-incident report within 72 hours. We can allow up to 8 hours/month per region as you suggested.

A couple of asks from our side:
- We need a commitment to a pilot traffic profile (QPS distribution + batching patterns) so our routing and autoscale configuration can be tuned; Marissa can send a short intake form.
- If the pilot expands to production, we would want to revert to the standard SLA (99.9%) or renegotiate long-term credits — provisional terms would not apply post-pilot.

I've attached a quick draft amendment (SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf) for internal review. Laura — can your team review the remedy table and limitation language and flag anything we should tighten before sending to Brightline legal?

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher | Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA floor adjustment for batched inference pilot

On Apr 18, 2028, at 12:05 PM, Sean Gallagher wrote:
> 
> - Pilot uptime floor: 99.5% for the 90-day pilot window (matches your request).
> - Remedy (monthly service credit): tiered scaling ... Cap at 20% of the monthly invoice for pilot months.

This reads reasonable as a commercial accommodation for a time-limited pilot. A few suggested edits to the amendment language before we send to Brightline procurement:

1) Definition clarity: explicitly define "Availability" as "successful token-generation responses within 5xx or timeouts excluded" and tie measurement to the regional metric for their primary region.
2) Remedy mechanics: specify that credits are calculated against the invoice for the affected region for the month of the incident and that credits are the sole and exclusive remedy (preserve limitation of liability).
3) Escrow/cap: include a sentence that the 20% cap is limited to the pilot term and will not set a precedent for future negotiated terms.
4) Termination for convenience: add a 30-day termination clause for either party during the pilot if operational profile materially deviates (we should require advance notice and churn protection language).

I'll inline suggested redlines into SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf and return by EOD. Marissa, please confirm operational intake items we need from Brightline and whether the 48-hour maintenance notice is workable for your team.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal & Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@brightline.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: 2028-04-19T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment: batched inference uptime floor and monthly credit cap

Sean / Laura —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the draft. The remedy tiers look fair and the 20% cap is acceptable for the pilot window. A few quick notes from procurement:
- We'll fill out the intake form today and share our QPS/batch distribution sample.
- Procurement asks that the credit calculation be expressed in the amendment as an absolute dollar amount example (we provided monthly spend estimate in the attached worksheet).
- We can accept the 48-hour scheduled maintenance notification but ask that you provide a monthly maintenance calendar if rolling updates are planned during the pilot.

Please send the redlines and an editable doc (DocuSign-ready) and we'll aim to return the signed amendment within 5 business days. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if anything is unclear.

Jordan
